Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
# Green Party 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Healthcare
The manifesto proposes £28bn additional annual NHS spending by 2030, plus £20bn capital investment over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteed GP access, universal NHS dentistry (£3bn annually by 2030), increased primary care funding, and a National Cancer Plan. Mental health provision would be expanded, with counsellors in all schools.

## Social Care
£20bn annual investment would fund free personal care for elderly and disabled people. The party proposes national pay structures for care workers and increased disability benefits by 5%.

## Housing
150,000 new social homes annually would be built, with the right-to-buy ended. Rent controls would be enabled for local authorities, and no-fault evictions ended. A £29bn five-year programme would retrofit homes for energy efficiency.

## Energy
Wind power would provide 70% of electricity by 2030. New oil and gas licences would be stopped, fossil fuel subsidies ended, and a carbon tax introduced at £120/tonne rising to £500. Community ownership of energy infrastructure would be expanded. Nuclear development would cease.

## Economy
£40bn average annual green investment is proposed, with railways, water companies, and major energy retailers returned to public ownership. A wealth tax of 1-2% on assets above £10m would be introduced, alongside aligned capital gains tax rates.

## Employment
A £15/hour minimum wage would apply to all ages. Maximum 10:1 pay ratios would be introduced. Anti-union legislation would be repealed, and gig workers given full employment rights.

## Welfare
Universal Credit would increase by £40 weekly. The two-child benefit cap would be abolished, and the five-week benefit wait ended.

## Environment
30% of land and sea would be protected by 2030. Water companies would be nationalised. A Rights of Nature Act would grant legal personhood to nature.

## Education
School funding would increase by £8bn, including teacher pay rises. University tuition fees would be scrapped and maintenance grants restored. Academies would return to local authority control.

## Transport
£10bn annual subsidies for rail and buses are proposed, with free bus travel for under-18s. Railways would be publicly owned. Petrol and diesel vehicle sales would end by 2027.

## Democracy
Proportional representation would replace first-past-the-post voting. Voting age would lower to 16. The House of Lords would become elected.

## Immigration
The hostile environment policy would end. Safe asylum routes would be established, with applicants permitted to work during processing.

## Foreign Policy
The manifesto calls for an immediate Israel-Gaza ceasefire, recognition of Palestine, and ending UK arms exports to Israel. Overseas aid would rise to 1% of GNI. The party supports rejoining the EU and signing the UN nuclear weapons prohibition treaty.

## Funding
Revenue would come from wealth taxes (£50-70bn annually by parliament's end), business taxes (£40bn over five years), and carbon taxes (up to £80bn annually by parliament's end).
